name: Sankey Leak
summary: A Minard-style flow of ribbons where the anomaly is a coral leak peeling off the checkout stage.
look: Warm paper, thin ink stage nodes and translucent teal ribbons with bezier curves; exits dissolve in grey gradients. The only saturated colour is the coral leak band.

components.name: Flow ribbon
components.role: cubic-bezier band, width = volume, teal at 55–90 % opacity

components.name: Stage node
components.role: thin ink bar with a bold stage label above it

components.name: Exit fade
components.role: gradient ribbon that dissolves = users who normally leave

components.name: Leak band
components.role: the one coral ribbon that is new since the deploy

components.name: Rule + callout
components.role: hairline rule separating the diagram from the numbers

components.name: Terminal button
components.role: the last node of the flow is the CTA itself

motion.name: Pour-through
motion.how: ribbon clip-path wipes left → right with power1.inOut 0.5 s per stage, one beat per stage at 120 BPM

motion.name: Braid snap
motion.how: ribbon endpoints tween to the knot with expo.inOut 0.75 s ending exactly on the drop

motion.name: Leak peel
motion.how: coral band grows from 0 to full width with elastic.out(1,0.6) 0.6 s on the snare; label types 30 ms/char

story: Hook: 38 grey ribbons tangle, a thin coral one hides inside. Drop: they braid into one knot where the Acme mark lands and a teal channel pours out. Proof: Visits → Cart → Checkout → Paid, a coral band leaks −18% since 09:42 after deploy #2231, Roll back. CTA: the channel bends into the Start free button.
adapt: Map your core funnel (signup → activate → pay, request → queue → worker) as three or four nodes and let the anomaly be a coloured band leaking from the stage that broke.

references.note: width-as-flow and Minard's 1869 Napoleon map lineage

fit.risk: Flow diagrams get unreadable fast; keep ≤ 4 stages and one coloured leak, everything else neutral.
